items.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Review.
items.summary: Comprehensive review of IBS diagnosis and treatment with prevalence of 7-16% in the US and annual direct costs over $1 billion.

items.title: Amitriptyline at Low-Dose and Titrated for Irritable Bowel Syndrome as Second-Line Treatment in primary care (ATLANTIS): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
items.summary: ATLANTIS trial found low-dose amitriptyline ineffective as second-line IBS treatment in primary care, missing primary endpoint.

items.title: Low-dose titrated amitriptyline as second-line treatment for adults with irritable bowel syndrome in primary care: the ATLANTIS RCT.
items.summary: Health technology assessment of the ATLANTIS trial confirming amitriptyline's lack of effectiveness for IBS in primary care.

items.title: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating the effectiveness of fecal microbiota transplantation for patients with irritable bowel syndrome.
items.summary: Meta-analysis of RCTs found fecal microbiota transplantation yielded inconsistent results for IBS treatment.

items.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in irritable bowel syndrome: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.summary: Meta-analysis showed no significant difference in short-term outcomes for FMT versus placebo in IBS patients.

items.title: Efficacy of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.summary: Meta-analysis of RCTs examining FMT efficacy in IBS with inconsistent results across studies.

items.title: Randomised clinical trial: effects of MD-7246 on irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea.
items.summary: Phase 2 RCT of MD-7246 (delayed-release linaclotide) for IBS-D evaluating efficacy and dose-response.

items.title: Randomized Clinical Trial: Crofelemer Treatment in Women With Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
items.summary: RCT of crofelemer in women with IBS-D evaluating effects on abdominal pain with post hoc FDA responder analysis.

items.title: Tegaserod for the Treatment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
items.journal: Anti-inflammatory & anti-allergy agents in medicinal chemistry
items.summary: Review noting tegaserod was withdrawn in 2007 due to increased cardiovascular risks despite being a 5-HT4 agonist for IBS-C.

items.title: Probiotic vs. Placebo in Irritable Bowel Syndrome:A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.journal: Middle East journal of digestive diseases
items.summary: RCT of Lactobacillus reuteri probiotic versus placebo in IBS patients using Rome III criteria.

items.title: Treatment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome by Chinese Medicine: A Review.
items.summary: Review of Chinese medicine treatments for IBS including prescriptions, acupuncture, and moxibustion with proposed mechanisms.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and gut microbiota.
items.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
items.summary: Review of gut microbiota's role in IBS pathogenesis and treatment, linking dysbiosis to symptoms and quality of life.

items.title: Management Options for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
items.summary: Review of IBS management options covering pathophysiology and novel treatment approaches including lifestyle and pharmacotherapy.

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Lifestyle modification as part of novel treatment approaches for IBS

pipelineDrugs.name: MD-7246
